ask: C11, POSIX. logread.c: memory-mapped log scanner. mmap a file, iterate length-prefixed binary records (u32 len + body) without reading the whole file, validate bounds, count by severity byte, print the last N records of a requested severity, and unmap cleanly on every exit path. write the file.
prose:
wrote `logread.c`. here's the rundown.

The scanner mmaps the file read-only with `MAP_PRIVATE` and closes the fd immediately after, since the kernel keeps its own reference until `munmap`. A single forward pass walks length-prefixed records: 4-byte little-endian body length, then the body. Each bounds check guards against truncated headers (`remaining < 4`) and truncated bodies (`body_len > remaining`), setting a corruption flag and breaking the loop rather than reading past the mapping.

`body[0]` is the severity byte (records with `body_len == 0` are skipped — no severity to read). Matches for the requested severity are collected into a small dynamic array storing pointers into the mapped region, so the last-N print pass just indexes backward from the end without re-scanning. Output is escaped (`\xNN` for non-printables) so binary payloads don't corrupt the terminal.

Cleanup paths: `munmap` runs on normal exit and after parse errors. The OOM path inside `matchvec_push` frees the match vector and unmaps before returning 1. `fstat` failure and non-regular files bail before mmap. Empty files print a message and exit 0.

Build and run:

```
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -o logread logread.c
./logread logfile.bin 3 20     # severity 3, last 20 records
```

Exit codes: `0` clean parse, `1` fatal (open/stat/mmap/oom), `2` truncated or corrupt data (still prints what it found before the break).
